title: NASA Awards L3Harris Contract to Build All Glass Telescope for LISA Mission
summary: L3Harris Technologies has been selected by NASA to design, assemble, integrate and test a telescope for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission.
body_markdown:
**ROCHESTER, N.Y., Oct. 8, 2026** — L3Harris Technologies (NYSE: LHX) has been selected by NASA to design, assemble, integrate and test a telescope for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission.


The European Space Agency will lead the mission, which aims to detect gravitational waves in space by measuring distance changes between satellites using laser beams to help better understand black holes, colliding stars and space-time.


“LISA will open a new window into the universe that ground-based observatories cannot access,” said Jeff Hanke, President, Space Systems, Space & Mission Systems, L3Harris. “By listening to the low-frequency ripples in space-time across millions of kilometers, LISA allows the study of massive, distant and rare cosmic events that are otherwise invisible.”


This mission will deploy three satellites in a heliocentric orbit, forming a triangular constellation spanning 2.5 million kilometers to measure distance changes smaller than the width of a single atom. Each satellite will include two L3Harris telescopes capable of transmitting and receiving precision laser beams with the support of ceramic glass.


L3Harris previously manufactured and assembled a full-scale prototype telescope for LISA that is guiding the development of flight hardware at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.
